# Medicare Enrollment Arizona (ECOS Medicare Solutions)

> Plain-English Medicare guidance for Arizona residents who are turning 65 or already enrolled. Covers Medicare Parts A, B, C and D, Medigap (Medicare Supplement), official 2026 costs, enrollment periods and deadlines, and free local help across Arizona. Operated by ECOS Medicare Solutions and Darin Weidauer, a licensed Medicare insurance agent, with offices in Mesa and Sun City, Arizona (appointments recommended). This site is NOT affiliated with or endorsed by the U.S. government, CMS, or the federal Medicare program. We do not offer every plan available in your area; contact Medicare.gov or 1-800-MEDICARE for all options.

Key facts (2026, source: U.S. Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services):
- Medicare Part B standard premium: $202.90/month; annual deductible: $283.
- Medicare Part A: $0 premium for most (40+ work quarters); $311/month with 30-39 quarters; $565/month with fewer than 30 quarters. Hospital deductible: $1,736 per benefit period. Days 61-90: $434/day. Lifetime reserve days: $868/day. Skilled nursing days 21-100: $217/day.
- Medicare Part D out-of-pocket prescription cap: $2,100 per year. A Medicare Prescription Payment Plan can spread costs monthly.
- Medicare Advantage (Part C) average national premium: about $14/month.
- IRMAA high-income surcharge starts above $109,000 (single) / $218,000 (married filing jointly), based on 2024 income.

Enrollment periods:
- Initial Enrollment Period (IEP): 7 months around your 65th birthday (3 months before, birthday month, 3 months after).
- Fall Open Enrollment / Annual Enrollment Period (AEP): October 15 - December 7; changes effective January 1.
- Medicare Advantage Open Enrollment Period: January 1 - March 31.
- General Enrollment Period (GEP): January 1 - March 31 (for those who missed the IEP; penalties may apply).
- Special Enrollment Periods (SEP): triggered by life events such as losing employer coverage (about 8 months for Part B).
- Medigap Open Enrollment: one-time 6-month window starting when you are 65 and enrolled in Part B (guaranteed acceptance).

Free, unbiased Arizona help: State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP), 1-800-432-4040. Federal help: 1-800-MEDICARE (1-800-633-4227), TTY 1-877-486-2048, 24/7. Compare and enroll: https://planenroll.com/?purl=Darin-Weidauer

## Arizona-specific facts
- Arizona's Medicaid programme is AHCCCS (Arizona Health Care Cost Containment System); long-term care is ALTCS.
- Arizona applies no asset/resource test to the Medicare Savings Programs; the AHCCCS eligibility chart lists the QMB, SLMB and QI-1 resource limit as not applicable. Only income is measured.
- ALTCS is an entitlement programme with no waiting list, unlike the waiver programmes many states run.
- AHCCCS requires its Complete Care and ALTCS contractors to operate a D-SNP in every service area where they hold a Medicaid contract.
- Arizona does NOT have a Medigap birthday rule. The initial six-month Medigap open enrolment window at 65 is therefore more consequential here.
